summary.text: A 57-year-old woman with no relevant past medical history was examined for about one year of recurrent vertigo with fluctuating right-ear hearing loss, tinnitus, nausea and vomiting. Examination and vestibular signs were normal, audiometry showed severe right and mild left sensorineural hearing loss, and she met criteria for definite unilateral Ménière’s disease. Six months of acetazolamide and betahistine gave only minimal improvement, so intratympanic dexamethasone was started.

Intratympanic dexamethasone with continued betahistine was followed by complete remission of vertigo for about one year. She then returned with sudden falls without warning or loss of consciousness and multiple contusions, consistent with vestibular drop attacks. After the second injection of a second dexamethasone course, a severe drop attack caused cranial trauma with a large extracranial hematoma; she developed marked anxiety, needed ambulation assistance and wore a protective helmet.

Given the severity and frequency of the drop attacks, intratympanic gentamicin was chosen after baseline caloric testing and vHIT within normal limits. Injections 7 days apart were stopped after the second when continuous vertigo and spontaneous left-beating nystagmus developed. Hearing thresholds worsened slightly, mainly at high frequencies. After gentamicin, caloric testing showed severe right-sided vestibular hypofunction and vHIT showed reduced right VOR gain with corrective saccades. One month later typical vertigo attacks had resolved.

At one year the drop attacks and vertigo had completely resolved, with no recurrence over two years of follow-up. She underwent several months of vestibular rehabilitation and reported only mild dizziness. Hearing thresholds returned close to baseline, VNG showed a small leftward nystagmus, and cVEMPs were absent on the right, which the authors say cannot be conclusively attributed to gentamicin. She remains on maintenance betahistine.

caption_evidence.quote:
Figure 1
Pure-tone audiogram obtained at presentation. Red circles represent right-ear air-conduction thresholds, and blue crosses represent left-ear air-conduction thresholds. The dashed green line represents bone-conduction thresholds. Frequencies are displayed in kHz on the horizontal axis and hearing thresholds in dB HL on the vertical axis. The audiogram at presentation shows severe sensorineural hearing loss in the right ear and mild sensorineural hearing loss in the left ear.

figures.caption_summary: Pure-tone audiogram at presentation: severe sensorineural hearing loss right, mild left.
figures.attribution_notes: Index-patient test recording or audiogram; the case text cites this figure for the index patient. Whole figure without printed panel letters.

caption_evidence.quote:
Figure 2
Video nystagmography (VNG) recording obtained at presentation, demonstrating the absence of spontaneous nystagmus. The upper panel shows horizontal eye position recordings, while the lower panel shows vertical eye position recordings (degrees) over time (seconds). Red and blue tracings represent recordings from each eye. No significant spontaneous horizontal or vertical ocular drift was observed during baseline examination. Eye movements were recorded using an Interacoustics videonystagmography system (Interacoustics A/S, Denmark).

figures.caption_summary: Baseline VNG recording at presentation: no spontaneous nystagmus.
figures.attribution_notes: Index-patient test recording or audiogram; the case text cites this figure for the index patient. Whole figure without printed panel letters.

caption_evidence.quote:
Figure 3
Monothermal caloric testing performed before intratympanic gentamicin therapy, showing preserved bilateral caloric reactivity. This baseline assessment was used as a screening evaluation of caloric responsiveness and should not be interpreted as a complete bithermal caloric test. The left panels show horizontal eye movement recordings during warm (44 °C) caloric irrigations. The right panels display the corresponding slow phase velocity (SPV) responses. Time is expressed in seconds and SPV in degrees per second (°/s). Caloric stimulation and eye movement recording were performed using an Interacoustics VNG system and caloric irrigator (Interacoustics A/S, Denmark).

figures.caption_summary: Monothermal (warm 44 °C) caloric testing before gentamicin: preserved bilateral reactivity.
figures.attribution_notes: Index-patient test recording or audiogram; the case text cites this figure for the index patient. Whole figure without printed panel letters.

caption_evidence.quote:
Figure 4
Video head impulse testing (vHIT) of the horizontal semicircular canals performed before intratympanic gentamicin therapy demonstrated preserved and relatively symmetrical vestibulo-ocular reflex (VOR) gain bilaterally, with a median VOR gain at 60 ms of 0.73 for the right horizontal canal and 0.91 for the left horizontal canal. No significant overt or covert corrective saccades were observed, consistent with normal lateral semicircular canal function. Testing was performed using an Interacoustics vHIT system (Interacoustics A/S, Denmark).

figures.caption_summary: Baseline vHIT of the horizontal canals before gentamicin with no significant corrective saccades.
figures.attribution_notes: Index-patient test recording or audiogram; the case text cites this figure for the index patient. Whole figure without printed panel letters.

caption_evidence.quote:
Figure 5
Video nystagmography (VNG) recording obtained after intratympanic gentamicin therapy, demonstrating intense spontaneous left-beating horizontal nystagmus, consistent with acute right-sided vestibular hypofunction induced by treatment. The upper panel shows horizontal eye position traces, while the lower panel shows vertical eye position recordings. Red and blue tracings represent recordings from each eye. The spontaneous nystagmus persisted in the absence of visual fixation and was associated with significant post-treatment vertigo and imbalance.

figures.caption_summary: VNG after gentamicin: intense spontaneous left-beating horizontal nystagmus.

Pure-tone audiometry performed after the second intratympanic gentamicin injection. PTA for the left ear remained stable at 19 dB HL, whereas PTA for the right ear increased from 61 dB HL before treatment to 74 dB HL after treatment, indicating a worsening of hearing thresholds in the treated ear. Red circles and connecting lines represent baseline (pre-treatment) air-conduction thresholds of the right ear, while black circles and gray connecting lines represent post-treatment right-ear air-conduction thresholds. Blue crosses and connecting lines represent baseline (pre-treatment) air-conduction thresholds of the left ear, while black crosses and gray connecting lines represent post-treatment left-ear air-conduction thresholds. Bithermal caloric testing performed after intratympanic gentamicin therapy, demonstrating severe right-sided vestibular hypofunction, with markedly reduced caloric responses on the right side and preserved responses on the left. Figure 10
Video nystagmography (VNG) recording obtained one year after intratympanic gentamicin therapy, demonstrating a small residual spontaneous left-beating horizontal nystagmus, consistent with persistent but compensated right-sided vestibular hypofunction. Cervical vestibular-evoked myogenic potential (cVEMP) testing performed one year after intratympanic gentamicin therapy.
